page.overview:
Who is Juliet Capulet?

Lord Capulet (Father) Lady Capulet (Mother)

Juliet seems quiet and obedient at first. She says very little and tells Lady Capulet that she will "look to like" when it comes to Count Paris.

However, when she meets Romeo, she comes out of her shell. She speaks as much as Romeo and in the same style. Her complex speech and thoughts show her intelligence. She is also very independent and brave in defying her father, going through with Friar Lawrence's plan and quickly taking her life, saying "I'll be brief."

She calls her mother 'Madam', which points at a distant relationship between them. This is made even more clear in contrast with the bond Juliet has with her nurse, whom she calls "honey-nurse".
